paragraphs.text: March 19. The Life of Our Venerable Father Paul the Simple.

The holy man of God Hierax, Cronius, and many other brothers of whom I wish to speak used to relate that a certain Paul, a farmer who worked the fields, was exceptionally innocent and simple in his way of life. He married a beautiful woman whose disposition was wicked. She sinned without his knowledge. After a long time, he unexpectedly came home from the fields and found them doing wrong, as providence was guiding Paul toward what would benefit him. And when he saw her with her usual lover, he laughed and called out to them, saying, “Well, well! By Jesus, I do not care about this! I will not see her anymore. Go on, keep her and her children, for I am leaving and will become a monk.” And without saying anything to anyone, he went into the desert to the blessed Anthony and knocked at the door. Saint Anthony came out and asked him what he wanted. Paul said, “I want to become a monk.” Anthony answered him, “You are sixty years old and already an old man. You cannot become a monk here. Instead, go to the village and make your living by working, giving thanks to God, for you cannot endure the hardships of the desert.” The old man answered, “Whatever you teach me, I will do.”

Anthony said to him, “I told you that you are old and cannot become a monk. If you want to become a monk, go and enter a communal monastery where there are more brothers who can care for you in your infirmities. For I live here alone, not eating any food until the fifth day, and even then only sparingly.” With these words he tried to send Paul away. And when he would not listen to him, Anthony shut the door and therefore did not go in [?] for three days, not even to relieve himself. But the old man stayed without leaving. On the fourth day, Anthony had an unavoidable bodily need. He opened the door and came out. Seeing Paul again, he said to him, “Go away from here, old man. Why do you press me? You cannot stay here.” Paul said to him, “I cannot go anywhere but here.” Anthony looked and saw that he had brought no provisions, neither bread nor water nor anything else, and that this was his fourth day enduring without food. He thought, “Perhaps he will collapse and die, since he is not accustomed to hunger, and this will harm my soul.” So he took him inside with him.

And the blessed and great Anthony, having thoroughly learned everything about him, that his soul was very perfect, and that the servant of Christ was very simple, after a few months, through the grace of Christ, with the help of the blessed Anthony as well, built him a separate cell so that he might undergo testing by demons. And Paul the Simple lived alone for one year, and was granted grace over demons and every kind of illness, having brought the gift of self-restraint to perfection. Now, on one of those days, a young man who was very violently possessed by a demon was brought to the blessed Anthony. When the great Anthony looked at the young man, he said to those bringing him, “This is not my task. For I have not yet been granted grace over this ruling order of demons. But this gift belongs to Paul the Simple.” And the great Anthony went to the tried and tested Paul, taking the young man along too, and said to him, “Father Paul, drive this demon out of this man, so that he may go back in good health to his own

home and glorify God.” Paul said to him, “And what about you?” Anthony said to him, “I am not free; I have other work.” And the great Anthony left the young man there and returned to his own cell. Then the innocent elder rose, prayed, and called the man who was [?], saying, “Father Anthony said, ‘Come out of the man.’” But the demon cried out blasphemously, saying, “I will not come out, you wicked, deceitful old man!” Then he took his sheepskin cloak and struck him on the back, saying, “Come out! Father Anthony said so.” But the demon uttered blasphemies against Anthony and Paul, saying all the more, “These hungry, insatiable men, who never have enough of their own! What dealings do you two have with me? Why are you tormenting us?” Paul said, “Will you come out, or shall I go to Christ? He will bring misery upon you.” But that savage demon blasphemed Christ too, crying out, “I will not come out!” Then Paul became angry with the demon and went out of his cell at midday. Now the heat of Egypt is in no way less fierce than that Babylonian

furnace. So the holy elder stood on a rock in the scorching heat and prayed to God, saying, “You see, Jesus Christ, who were crucified under Pontius Pilate, that I will not come down from this rock, nor will I eat or drink until I die, unless you hear me and drive this demon out of this man and set him free from this unclean spirit.” While the simple-hearted and humble-minded Paul, who belonged to Jesus, was still speaking, before the prayer was finished, the demon cried aloud, “I am going! I am going! I am coming out by force, driven by torment. I am leaving the man. Never again will I come near the humble-minded and simple-hearted Paul. For he drives me away, and I do not know where I am going.” And immediately the demon came out and turned into a great serpent, about seventy cubits long, and went crawling toward the Red Sea, so that what was spoken by the Holy Spirit might be fulfilled: “On whom shall I look, if not on the one who is meek and quiet and humble in heart, and who trembles at my

words?” These are the miracles of the humble and simple-hearted Paul, and there were others greater and mightier than these. He was called ‘the Simple’ by all the brothers. Through his prayers, may we become sharers in the kingdom of heaven, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
